item.title: Suns’ Khaman Maluach puts Jabari Smith Jr. on a poster with monster dunk
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Suns’ Khaman Maluach puts Jabari Smith Jr. on a poster with monster dunk appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Phoenix Suns big man Khaman Maluach put his size to good use, at the expense of Houston Rockets forward Jabari Smith Jr., during an NBA Cup matchup between West Group A teams at the Toyota Center in Houston. The former Duke Blue Devils star center Maluach put Smith on a poster with a powerful two-handed throwdown and even drew a foul. Here is a look at that play. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) OH MY MAN MAN 😳 pic.twitter.com/25iiNdIa6c — Phoenix Suns (@Suns) November 26, 2026 That dunk capped an excellent two-man play between Maluach and Suns star shooting guard Devin Booker. After Booker refused the screen from Maluach, the big man simply rolled to the basket and was rewarded for his great off-the-ball movement with a nice pass from Booker. By the time Smith reacted, it was too late to stop Maluach from punishing the rim. More than Maluach’s dunk, the way the Suns set up that play was quite a delicious watch for basketball fans. At 7-foot-2 and just 20 years old, Maluach is still oozing with promise. He’s barely scratched the surface of his potential, and the Suns must be excited to see what kind of player he becomes as he continues to gain experience in the pros. Interestingly, the Rockets selected Maluach 10th overall in the first round of the 2025 NBA Draft before packaging him in a trade to the Suns that sent future Basketball Hall of Famer Kevin Durant to Houston. In his first 16 games in the 2026-27 NBA season, Maluach averaged 7.7 points, 5.6 rebounds and 0.9 blocks, while shooting 63.3 percent from the field. The Suns entered the game with a 9-7 record and were looking to beat the Rockets for the second time this season. item.title: Chad Smith wears Wu-Tang Nikes to meet group; Lions unveil Wu merch
item.description: Chad Smith showed up for soundcheck at Ford Field for his Thanksgiving performance with the Wu-Tang Clan wearing Wu-Tang branded Nike Dunks, the Lions showed in an Instagram video released Nov. 25. Smith, the Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer who grew up in Bloomfield Hills, is set to join the Wu during their halftime performance during the Lions-Bears game on Nov. 26. The performance is curated by Eminem and Paul Rosenberg, who are in their second year of a three-year agreement to steer the Thanksgiving halftime show. More: Eminem's manager, Paul Rosenberg, calls Wu-Tang halftime 'a bullseye' In the video, Smith is seen greeting members of the Wu-Tang Clan, the legendary New York rap collective that was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame earlier this month. Smith is complimented on his kicks, a pair of black and yellow Nike Dunk high-tops branded with the Wu-Tang logo. The shoes were originally released in extremely limited edition in 1999, and were rereleased in 2024 for their 25th anniversary. "I'm representin', oh yeah!" Smith says, before Wu-Tang's Method Man says to the camera, "now who else can hang out with a Chili Pepper?" View this post on Instagram Wu-Tang was announced as the halftime performer on Nov. 1 . Paul Rosenberg, Eminem's manager, told The Detroit News the selection of Wu-Tang is "a bullseye" in terms of what he and Eminem want for the show. "When the idea of Wu-Tang came up, we just all thought A) it's going to be really unexpected, which we love, and B) we thought it was a bullseye for the right sort of association with the thing that Marshall and myself are passionate about, which his hip-hop," he said . "The idea of a Wu-Tang Thanksgiving seems so awesome that we went for it." Smith was announced as a guest performer with the Staten Island group on Nov. 20 . "Obviously Chad being from Michigan and being a huge Lions fan, it just made sense, and the band loved the idea as well," Rosenberg said. The Lions also unveiled several specialized Wu-Tang merch items that will be available at Thursday's game. They include a Wu-Tang Lions shirt (which reads "Shaolin to the Motor City" on the back), a Wu-Tang Forever T-shirt with a Lions logo at the center, and a Wu-Tang/ Lions crossover hoodie and crew neck sweatshirt. (To see the items, scroll to slide 5 in the post below.) View this post on Instagram The Wu-Tang/ Lions merchandise will be available at the game at Lions Supply inside Gate A, according to the Instagram post. Kickoff for Thursday's game is scheduled for 1:02 p.m. agraham@detroitnews.com This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Chad Smith wears Wu-Tang Nikes to meet group; Lions unveil Wu merch

item.title: Nets topple Bucks in NBA Cup clash to snap five-game skid
item.description: The teams with the two worst records in the Eastern Conference faced each other Wednesday night in Milwaukee, but no one needed to accuse either the Nets or the Bucks of tanking in this one. Neither team can win the draft lottery after the season because both franchises essentially traded their respective 2027 first-round picks years ago, but the Nets at least halted their five-game losing streak with a defensively improved 104-97 victory in an NBA Cup game at Fiserv Forum. Julius Randle netted a team-high 28 points as the Nets (4-13) posted their first NBA Cup victory after losses earlier in the season against the Pistons and the Magic. Michael Porter Jr. was held to 12 points on 4-for-14 shooting with 11 rebounds to follow another quiet scoring night (11) Monday in Minnesota. Julius Randle, who scored a team-high points, shoots a floater during the Nets’ 104-97 win over the Bucks on Nov. 25, 2026, in Milwaukee. Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Egor Dëmin had an active game with 14 points and a plus-15 rating in 25 minutes off the bench. Noah Clowney nailed three 3-pointers among his 17 points, and Day’Ron Sharpe contributed 11 points, 14 boards and five assists for the Nets. Tyler Herro, who had a career-best 50-point game Saturday against the 76ers, scored 21 of his 28 points in the second half for the Bucks (2-17). “We’ve lost a few in a row, so we’ve gotta try to get a win no matter who we’re playing against,” Porter told the YES Network before the game. “They’re an NBA team. They are at the bottom of the standings right now, but so are we, so it’s gonna be a dogfight, and we gotta try to get out of here with a win.” The NBA instituted rule changes in the offseason to discourage tanking for draft position, essentially penalizing the teams with the worst three records in the league with lower odds to secure the No. 1 overall pick in the lottery. The Nets’ 2027 first-round pick is controlled by the Rockets from an unprotected pick swap as part of Brooklyn’s deal to acquire James Harden in January 2021. The Bucks, who dealt away superstar forward Giannis Antetokounmpo to the Heat over the summer, also had committed to a pick swap involving their 2027 first-rounder when they acquired guard Jrue Holiday from New Orleans in 2020. The Nets had allowed at least 70 points in the first half four times during their five-game skid, but this slow start was more due to offensive inefficiency. Noah Clowney, who scored 17 points off the bench, puts up a shot during the second quarter of the Nets’ road win over the Bucks. Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Brooklyn missed five of its first six shots and spotted the Bucks a 9-2 lead in the first three minutes. But Porter knocked down two straight 3s and scored eight as part of a 15-1 run to vault the Nets into an eight-point advantage en route to a 28-24 edge through 12 minutes. A 3-pointer by Clowney and a jumper by Randle extended the cushion to 10 early in the second. The Nets led by as many as 13 before the Bucks closed

item.description: Long before he reached the global stage, Kongklai Sor Sommai had already mastered the art of the comeback. He lost the first 10 bouts of his career, then rattled off 18 straight wins. Back-to-back defeats are hardly the deepest hole he has climbed out of, and his next turnaround begins against fellow Thai Worapon Lukjaoporongtom in the bantamweight Muay Thai co-main event of The Inner Circle 40 on Friday, November 27. The card goes down live in Asia primetime from Bangkok’s Lumpinee Stadium, exclusively for members at live.onefc.com . Stoppages of Ferrari Fairtex and Mohammad “Prince of Persia” Habibpour bookended a hard-fought win over Kendu Irving , giving him three consecutive victories and his best run in ONE. Then came a pair of painful setbacks. Julio Lobo outpointed him at The Inner Circle 12 in May, before Adam “El Capitano” Benwarwar survived two knockdowns to stop him in the second round at The Inner Circle 22 in July. Looking back on both losses, Kongklai admits his eagerness to entertain sometimes got the better of him. In the weeks since, he has worked to close the gaps in his armor. The Sor Sommai slugger told onefc.com: “For this camp, my team focused extra attention on my defense because my opponent is also a southpaw with a dangerous high kick. “I keep reminding myself not to get careless or repeat the same mistakes. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Seattle Mariners were one of the biggest disappointments in MLB last season. Coming off a 2025 season in which they were one win away from making it to the World Series for the first time in franchise history, they struggled during all of 2026 and missed the postseason entirely after winning just 76 games. And while the biggest problem point for the Mariners is their offense, that should not preclude them from making improvements to the other parts of the roster. In fact, they have been looking to improve their bullpen immensely with the signing of Adrian Morejon. As per Ben Nicholson-Smith of Sportsnet, the Mariners have thrown their hat into what is becoming a very crowded ring in the Morejon sweepstakes. Around five to six teams are believed to be in the running for Morejon’s services, which will undoubtedly drive up the price it would take to get the 27-year-old to sign on the dotted line. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Nicholson-Smith tweeted out that some see the Yankees as the favorite to sign Morejon, although that should not deter the Mariners at all from going after one of the best relief arms on the market. Morejon has blossomed into one of the best late-game arms in the big leagues. Over the past three seasons, he has turned into a devastating setup man for the San Diego Padres. Since 2024, Morejon is sporting a 2.58 ERA in 211 appearances off the bullpen. He pitched in 223.1 innings during that span, showing that he can go more than one inning if need be, and he struck out 248 total batters as well. item.title: Timberwolves Lose Another Star to Injury
item.description: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The Minnesota Timberwolves came off a long stretch at home to travel to Oklahoma City on Thanksgiving Eve for an NBA Cup game against the Thunder. Chris Finch’s team entered at 13-5, including 4-2 on the road, and had won its first two Group B games in the NBA Cup . Despite their playoff struggles against the Thunder, the Wolves came away with the win. Moving to 3-0 in NBA Cup play came at a cost. Already without Anthony Edwards and Donte DiVincenzo , Minnesota could now be without LaMelo Ball too. LaMelo Ball hurts ankle late for MN Timberwolves Minnesota came out strong against the Thunder, racing out to a 26-16 lead . The Wolves gave it back in the second quarter but responded in the second half and down the stretch. Then, with 2:29 left, LaMelo Ball rolled his left ankle after landing on Isaiah Hartenstein’s foot. LaMelo Ball grabbing left ankle and needs to be helped off the floor. He’s in a LOT of pain. — Jon Krawczynski (@JonKrawczynski) November 25, 2026 Finch didn’t have an update after the game. “It looked pretty bad but I’m not sure,” Finch said, according to Alan Horton (Wolves Radio) . Before the injury, Ball had played 29 minutes , scoring 19 points on 7-of-18 shooting with seven rebounds and eight assists while running the offense. He had played in all 19 games for Minnesota. He played 72 games last year but averaged just 35 per season in the three years before that. Related: Two Key Timberwolves Added to Injury Report The MN Timberwolves have looked for a facilitating point guard since Ricky Rubio left. Ball is the best mix of star power and prime-age talent they have had at the position since then, and he has kept Finch’s rotation afloat without DiVincenzo and Edwards. If the ankle injury isn’t significant, Ball may not miss much time. While he’s out, Ayo Dosunmu should get plenty of run at the point, and DiVincenzo’s return becomes even more important. Related: Timberwolves Lose Jaylen Clark for at Least Two Weeks Bones Hyland has run plenty of point with the second unit, and his minutes should grow if Ball misses an extended stretch. item.description: Credit: Matthew O’Haren-Imagn Images Penn State football flips 2027 QB from Boston College appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Penn State football has a new quarterback on board for the 2027 recruiting class, as three-star prospect Ben Rolapp flipped his commitment to the Nittany Lions from Boston College, On3’s Hayes Fawcett reported Wednesday night. His addition gives Penn State a new pledge at the position after losing its previous quarterback commit, Will Wood, to the Eagles last month. Wood initially committed to the Nittany Lions in May before switching to Boston College in late October. His connection with Eagles head coach Bill O’Brien, who previously led Penn State, played a role in that decision. The Nittany Lions subsequently pursued Missouri commit Braylen Warren, with head coach Matt Campbell traveling to Omaha, Nebraska, during the team’s bye week to extend an offer in person. However, Warren decided to remain with the Tigers, forcing Penn State to explore other options. The Nittany Lions eventually turned their attention to Rolapp, extending him an offer on October 28. The Connecticut native had originally committed to Boston College in June after attending a camp with O’Brien and his coaching staff. His decision to visit Penn State on November 22-23 came shortly after Brunswick School completed its undefeated season. Across the season, the 6-foot-2, 215-pound quarterback completed 138 of 198 attempts for 2,607 yards, 25 touchdowns and four interceptions. He also contributed 257 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns. item.title: No. 2 Ludlowe completes its first unbeaten regular season with victory over rival Warde
item.description: Fairfield Ludlowe quarterback Ryan Love runs for a touchdown in the second half against Fairfield Warde on November 24, 2026. (Arnold Gold/Hearst Connecticut M) FAIRFIELD - The Ludlowe football team finished what no Falcons squad had before it - an unbeaten regular season - with a 28-15 win over rival Warde on Wednesday night, earning one of the top two seeds in the upcoming Class L playoffs. The Falcons (10-0) have now qualified for the state tournament three straight years, but will host a CIAC playoff game as the higher seed for the first time in program history and attempt to earn the school's first postseason win. "10-0 means the world to me. I have been working with these kids since first grade and started playing tackle in fifth grade," Ludlowe quarterback Ryan Love said. "To see the whole town come together for a game is just bigger than football. Even if they are wearing red, it's a great atmosphere and I am so grateful I got to play in this game." More than 3,800 fans packed Taft Field to watch Ludlowe earn its seventh straight win in the series and keep the Gallagher/Banyas Trophy with the Falcons. Warde leads the all-time series 17-15. "Who would have thought 10 years ago, when I took the job and was told outright that we would never be .500?" Ludlowe coach Mitch Ross said. "It has been a lot of work, but it has been a labor of love. I love the players, love the coaches and they put everything into it." Ludlowe, ranked No. 2 in the GametimeCT Top 10 Football Poll, will be one of the top two seeds in the Class L tournament, where it lost in the quarterfinals in each of the past two seasons. It will have to wait for the result of Naugatuck's game Thursday before knowing its seed and opponent. "We will never forget that we have never won a playoff game here," Love said. "We haven't proved anything in the postseason and I know this team can prove a lot this postseason. I think we can make a run. The sky is the limit for this team." Warde was eliminated from playoff contention with the loss, but finished 6-4 in the first season under coach Steve Christy. "I am just so proud of this team," Christy said. "The senior class has set the stage for us. The way we fought today. We easily could have fallen over, but I thought we showed a lot of guts." Ludlowe led 14-0 at halftime on touchdown passes from Love to Timmy O'Neil and Jackson Danylko, then took a 21-0 lead in the third quarter on a 16-yard run from Love. Warde got on the board in the third on a pass from Luke Mancuso to AJ Cortina. Love ran for another touchdown from 34 yards out in the fourth quarter, and the scoring was capped by Warde's Dylan Osserman's 3-yard run. item.title: Jannik Sinner ruled out of Australian Open as injury lay-off continues
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Italian tennis player Jannik Sinner looks at the ball during his men's singles first-round match against Germany's Yannick Hanfmann at the Terra Wortmann Open tennis tournament. (is associated with: «Jannik Sinner ruled out of Australian Open as injury lay-off continues») David Inderlied/dpa Jannik Sinner will miss the Australian Open after undergoing knee surgery. The world number two has not played since defending his Wimbledon title in July and will now miss the first Grand Slam tournament of 2027. Tennis Australia chief executive Andrew Abdo said in a statement: "We've been in regular touch with Jannik's team and they've confirmed he won't be joining us for the Australian Open in January following his recent surgery. "Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for the Australian Open in 2028." The Italian confirmed on Tuesday he had undergone minor surgery after experiencing ongoing pain in his right knee. Sinner said in a statement earlier this week: "Over the past few months, together with my team, we've tried everything to treat my injury without surgery. "After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn't respond as we had all hoped, that's why today I underwent a minor surgery to improve the condition of my iliotibial band. "I really miss being on court and will now begin my recovery process together with my team." The iliotibial band is a thick band of fibrous connective tissue running down the outside of the thigh, and injuries associated with it are typically caused by overuse. Prior to his injury, the 25-year-old had a stellar start to 2026 which saw him win the first five Masters 1000 tournaments of the year, becoming the second man after Novak Djokovic to achieve the Golden Masters. His absence has allowed Alexander Zverev to overtake him in the world rankings, with Carlos Alcaraz in third place. Both men shared their well-wishes after Sinner's surgery. "The decision of making the surgery, I think his team made a good decision. He's young, has a lot of years ahead of him. I'm sure he's going to come back even stronger, even better," Alcaraz said on Wednesday. Zverev added: ""We know that he's mentally strong. I hope that he takes every step serious and that, in three, four months' time, he can be back to 100 per cent and be back playing."

item.description: 'Everyone who gave me grief': Ben Stokes' cheeky take on Shubman Gill ending 1st IND vs NZ Test early evokes Manchester memories originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Ben Stokes revisited the Manchester handshake controversy after the first India vs New Zealand Test ended early. He noted Shubman Gill's concern over Daryl Mitchell being on 49 before the batter initiated the handshake. The former England captain cheekily hit back at critics of his own early handshake against India in 2025. MORE: ‘Absolutely pathetic’: Stokes, Morgan criticise India over early draw with NZ What did Ben Stokes say about Shubman Gill's handshake against New Zealand? India vs New Zealand Test match in Wellington saw an early draw, reminding people of the 2025 Manchester Test, where Ben Stokes was criticised by many for handing India an early handshake. A post on Instagram regarding the current situation indicated that Ben would be happy with how things went down. "Really like how Gill actually thought Mitchell is on 49 and might not shake hands but Mitchell just came forward himself. Ben Stokes would be happy," the post said. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Cricket in Blood (@summmyyy_x) Discussing the issue in an episode of That's Not Cricket , Ben explained that Gill seemed afraid that Mitchell wouldn't shake hands while scoring 49 runs and then stepped forward of his own accord, ending the game at 239/5. "There was a lot of debate around that and I think this is now in front of me because what's happened is Shubman Gill of the Indian cricket team are in a position that we were as a team there in a result that was going to be a draw." He continued, "And he was hoping that the opposition would shake hands so he could get his team off the field. But he thinks that someone being on 49, close to a landmark, means that they are not going to." Stokes even took a dig at his critics. "Can we just say that everyone who reacted gave me a little grief. Can we get a reaction to Shubman Gill shaking hands and Daryl Mitchell doing the right thing by shaking hands when there cannot be a result? Thanks, Daryl." MORE: Christchurch pitch for India vs NZ 2nd Test: Will bowlers get assistance? What happened during the first India vs New Zealand Test in Wellington? item.title: College basketball expert calls Mark Pope a ‘major disappointment’
item.description: Kentucky Basketball is off to a disappointing start to the 2026-27 season, and the criticism surrounding Mark Pope and his program continues to grow following consecutive losses to Kansas by 20 points and Indiana by 14 points. NBC Sports college basketball analyst John Fanta recently shared his thoughts on the state of Kentucky basketball, and he didn’t hold back when discussing the third year of the Pope era. “Let’s just call it what it is: the Mark Pope era, to this point, has been a disappointment,” Fanta said. Fanta questioned Kentucky’s defensive scheme, physicality, and overall roster construction, pointing to the Wildcats’ struggles to stop opposing teams throughout the early portion of the season. “Their defensive scheme, I’m not sure what it is. Scheme would be an exaggeration for what it actually is. They couldn’t stop anybody early in the season. They couldn’t stop Northern Arizona. They weren’t going to stop Indiana. Milan Momcilovic, a winning player at a winning program, a lot is now on his shoulders. Too much is on his shoulders for a team with the kind of money that they possess. Their guards, not sturdy enough, not physical enough,” Fanta said. He also questioned whether Kentucky has the type of players necessary to meet the program’s traditional expectations. “When I think of Kentucky, I think of enforcers. They’re not that. I like Malachi Moreno, but I look at this Kentucky roster, and I compare it to the resources that they are reported to have available. Mark Pope is not getting it done there.” Fanta continued his criticism by pointing to the expectations that come with coaching at Kentucky and the amount of money reportedly invested in the roster. “To me, it comes off as he’s trying to be someone that he actually isn’t at a very difficult job. It’s a hard job because they have high expectations, but you are judged on your record,” he continued. “They had to claw just to get past Santa Clara in the NCAA Tournament with a $20 million roster. They spent a ton of money again. They’re not getting it done.” Fanta ultimately believes Kentucky may need to make a change if things don’t turn around, calling the current state of the program a major disappointment. “The Mark Pope era is a major disappointment, and Kentucky is going to have to make a change. … It’s just a brutal start to their season, and that fanbase has every right to be upset because, at Kentucky, if you want to be categorized as a blue blood—which the playing field has been level—it’s a very, very big disappointment.” With Kentucky now facing increased pressure following its losses to Kansas and Indiana, Pope and the Wildcats have plenty of work to do to get the season back on track.

The Cougars’ 38 attempts from beyond the arc set a new single-game Maui Invitational record, and the 17 makes tied the 2014 Cougars for the event’s second-highest mark. Providence was surrendering just 64 points per game before Wednesday. item.description: ©Credits: Getty Don’t poke the bear, especially when the bear is LeBron James. Bam Adebayo had a playful warning for his good friend after LeBron chose the Philadelphia 76ers over the Miami Heat in free agency, but James had the last laugh in their first matchup of the 2026-27 season. James delivered a triple-double with 25 points, 10 rebounds, and 12 assists as the 76ers defeated Miami 111-104 on Wednesday night. The victory also ended the Heat’s seven-game winning streak, giving Philadelphia a memorable result in the first meeting between the former Olympic teammates since James chose to take his talents to Philadelphia. Adebayo still had a productive night, finishing with 17 points and 11 rebounds. But his team could not stop James and the 76ers from securing the win. The Heat's momentum just hit a wall, and Adebayo's confidence may have cost Miami dearly. Stay locked in with EssentiallySports for every twist in the playoff race. When James chose Philadelphia over Miami during the offseason, Adebayo made it clear that their friendship would not stop him from competing against the four-time NBA champion. Speaking to reporters during a community back-to-school event in Miami on July 28, Adebayo revealed the message he sent James after learning of his decision. However, he first made sure to clarify that there were no hard feelings. “There ain’t no disappointment,” Adebayo said, per the Miami Herald. “To me, you should always be happy for a person and their decision. He made a decision where he feels like it’s his best situation to win. And I feel like I’m a good friend of LeBron’s.” The Heat star then revealed the playful warning he had delivered privately. “Like I told him in the message, I’m going to bust his a**,” Adebayo added. “So, it’s going to be an exciting season. I’m excited for the East. We got a whole new turnaround in the East. So, it’s going to be exciting this year.” The two developed a friendship through their time with Team USA, sharing the court during the 2024 Paris Olympics. Both played important roles in the Americans’ gold-medal run, fostering a relationship that extends beyond their NBA careers. That made Adebayo’s message less about resentment over James choosing another team and more about the competitive banter between friends. Still, the first opportunity to back up those words arrived Wednesday, and James made sure Philadelphia came away with the victory. LeBron James answers with Triple-Double as 76ers end Miami’s win streak James delivered his best performance of the season yet, recording 25 points, 12 assists, and 10 rebounds in Philadelphia’s 111-104 win. It was his first triple-double as a member of the 76ers and the 126th of his regular-season career. At 41 years and 330 days old, James also became the oldest player in NBA history to record a triple-double. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup.
